a: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites
p: The Hebrew names thirteen men and "the Levites." 2 Esdras has only three names. 1 Esdras has thirteen and calls them the Levites.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: and Jeshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah ... Pelaiah, and the Levites
readings.plain: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites

readings.w: 1 Esdras (Esdras A, the freer Greek parallel), Rahlfs' text, checked, 9:48 (Ἰησοῦς καὶ Ἀννιουθ καὶ Σαραβιας ... καὶ Φαλιας οἱ Λευῖται)
readings.orig: Ἰησοῦς καὶ Ἀννιουθ καὶ Σαραβιας ... καὶ Φαλιας οἱ Λευῖται
readings.en: Jesus and Anniuth and Sarabias ... and Phalias, the Levites
readings.plain: Jeshua, Anniuth, Sarabias and the rest, who were the Levites,

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (Ἰησοῦς καὶ Βαναιας καὶ Σαραβια)
readings.orig: καὶ Ἰησοῦς καὶ Βαναιας καὶ Σαραβια ... ἦσαν συνετίζοντες
readings.en: and Jesus and Banaias and Sarabia ... were instructing

why: The Hebrew "and the Levites" can mean "along with the other Levites," or the "and" can be read as "that is," which is how 1 Esdras takes it: the thirteen are themselves Levites. The short list of 2 Esdras is probably a scribe's shortening. The Plain keeps the Hebrew. Several of the same names lead the Levites in 9:4–5 and 10:9–13.

a: explaining it as they went. They set out its meaning
p: In the Hebrew "they" read and explained it. 2 Esdras makes Ezra the teacher.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: distinctly, and gave the sense
readings.plain: explaining it as they went. They set out its meaning

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ ἐδίδασκεν Ἔσδρας καὶ διέστελλεν ἐν ἐπιστήμῃ κυρίου)
readings.orig: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν Ἔσδρας καὶ διέστελλεν ἐν ἐπιστήμῃ κυρίου
readings.en: and Ezra taught and made it distinct in the knowledge of the Lord
readings.plain: and Ezra taught them and set it out clearly in the knowledge of the Lord

why: The Greek seems to have read the Hebrew letters differently and to have added Ezra's name, which the verse does not need. The Hebrew fits 8:7, where the Levites do the teaching. The note on this verse gives the views on what "explaining" meant.

a: Then Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe,
p: The Hebrew names Nehemiah "the governor." 2 Esdras has his name without the title. 1 Esdras has "Attarates" (Attharates in Codex Alexandrinus and in Rahlfs' text), its form of the title, and no Nehemiah.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.orig: וַיֹּאמֶר נְחֶמְיָה הוּא הַתִּרְשָׁתָא וְעֶזְרָא הַכֹּהֵן הַסֹּפֵר
readings.en: And Nehemiah, which is the Tirshatha, and Ezra the priest the scribe
readings.plain: Then Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe,

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ εἶπεν Νεεμιας καὶ Ἔσδρας ὁ ἱερεὺς καὶ γραμματεύς)
readings.orig: καὶ εἶπεν Νεεμιας καὶ Ἔσδρας ὁ ἱερεὺς καὶ γραμματεύς
readings.en: and Nehemiah and Ezra the priest and scribe said
readings.plain: Then Nehemiah, Ezra the priest and scribe,

readings.w: 1 Esdras (Esdras A, the freer Greek parallel), Rahlfs' text, checked, 9:49 (καὶ εἶπεν Ἀτθαράτης Ἔσδρᾳ τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ καὶ ἀναγνώστῃ), with Codex Alexandrinus (Ατθαρατης, Swete's notes); Codex Vaticanus (Swete) spells the name Ἀτταρατή, Attarates
readings.orig: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀτθαράτης Ἔσδρᾳ τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ καὶ ἀναγνώστῃ καὶ τοῖς Λευίταις
readings.en: and Attharates said to Ezra the chief priest and reader and to the Levites
readings.plain: Then the governor said to Ezra the high priest and reader,

why: Every Hebrew manuscript names Nehemiah. 1 Esdras, which tells Ezra's story without Nehemiah at all, turns the Hebrew title tirshata into a personal name, Attarates (Attharates in Alexandrinus), and so does not show that its Hebrew lacked Nehemiah's name. 2 Esdras, which has the name without the title, suggests to some that "who was the governor" was added, and to others that it was dropped. The Plain keeps the Hebrew. On what the joint mention means for the dating, see the note on 12:26.

a: because the joy of the LORD is your stronghold
t: "The joy of the LORD," "he," or "he will glorify you"?
p: Only the Hebrew has "the joy of the LORD." 2 Esdras has "for he is your strength," and 1 Esdras has "for the Lord will glorify you."

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: for the joy of the LORD is your strength
readings.plain: because the joy of the LORD is your stronghold

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ μὴ διαπέσητε, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἰσχὺς ὑμῶν)
readings.en: for he is your strength

readings.w: 1 Esdras (Esdras A, the freer Greek parallel), Rahlfs' text, checked, 9:52 (ὁ γὰρ κύριος δοξάσει ὑμᾶς)
readings.en: for the Lord will glorify you
readings.plain: for the Lord will honor you

why: Chedvah, "joy," is a rare, Aramaic-like word, found elsewhere only in 1 Chronicles 16:27 and Ezra 6:16. The literal 2 Esdras may have lacked it in its Hebrew copy, or shortened the line to "he is your strength." 1 Esdras paraphrases freely throughout this chapter. Every Hebrew manuscript has "the joy of the LORD," and the Plain follows it.

a: It is you who are the LORD, and you alone. You made the heavens
p: The Greek begins the prayer with "And Ezra said." The Hebrew has no new speaker, so the Levites of 9:5 go on speaking.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: Thou, even thou, art LORD alone; thou hast made heaven
readings.plain: It is you who are the LORD, and you alone. You made the heavens

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ εἶπεν Ἔσδρας Σὺ εἶ αὐτὸς κύριος μόνος); followed by the RSV and NRSV
readings.orig: καὶ εἶπεν Ἔσδρας Σὺ εἶ αὐτὸς κύριος μόνος· σὺ ἐποίησας τὸν οὐρανὸν
readings.en: And Ezra said: You are the Lord alone; you made the heaven
readings.plain: And Ezra said: It is you who are the LORD, and you alone. You made the heavens

why: The Greek may preserve an early reading, or a scribe may have added Ezra's name to give the great prayer a known author, as was done for other prayers. Ezra is not mentioned anywhere else in 9:1–10:39. The Plain follows the Hebrew, in which the Levites lead the prayer (see the setting card).

a: They made their necks stiff, and in their rebellion they appointed a leader to go back to their slavery
p: The Hebrew has bemiryam, "in their rebellion." The Greek has "in Egypt," which in Hebrew differs by one letter (bemitsrayim).

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008) (בְּמִרְיָם); KJV
readings.en: and in their rebellion appointed a captain to return to their bondage
readings.plain: They made their necks stiff, and in their rebellion they appointed a leader to go back to their slavery

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ ἔδωκαν ἀρχὴν ἐπιστρέψαι εἰς δουλείαν αὐτῶν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ); some Hebrew manuscripts are reported to read בְּמִצְרַיִם; NRSV
readings.en: and they appointed a leader to return to their slavery in Egypt
readings.plain: They made their necks stiff, and they appointed a leader to go back to their slavery in Egypt

why: The prayer echoes the people's words in the wilderness, "Let's appoint a leader and go back to Egypt" (Numbers 14:4), which favors "Egypt." But "rebellion" is the harder reading and makes good sense, and a scribe who knew Numbers could easily have changed it to "Egypt." The meaning is the same either way. The Plain keeps the Hebrew. The report of Hebrew manuscripts with "Egypt" comes from the printed apparatus and was not checked here.

p: The letters read Nobai, the margin Nebai. The Greek agrees with the letters.

readings.w: Ketiv (the letters written in the Masoretic Text); Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (Νωβαι)
readings.en: Nobai

readings.w: Qere (the reading in the margin of the Masoretic Text); KJV
readings.en: Nebai

why: The two forms differ by one letter (waw or yod), which scribes often confused. The written form has the support of the Greek (Νωβαι), so the Plain follows it, as book.json's policy for names says. The man is otherwise unknown.

t: "Son of Haggedolim" missing in the Greek
p: The Hebrew gives Zabdiel's father as Haggedolim. 2 Esdras ends the verse with the name Badiel and gives no father.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV, BSB
readings.en: Zabdiel, the son of one of the great men (KJV)

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (ἐπίσκοπος ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν Βαδιηλ)
readings.en: overseer over them, Badiel

why: The Greek shortens the lists of chapters 11–12 often (see the note on 11:16), so its lack of the father's name is probably part of that pattern. Whether Haggedolim is a name or a description is discussed in the note on this verse.

p: The margin has the usual spelling of the singer's name. The letters spell it Jedithun.

readings.w: Qere (the reading in the margin of the Masoretic Text)
readings.en: Jeduthun

readings.w: Ketiv (the letters written in the Masoretic Text)
readings.en: Jedithun

why: Both spellings appear for David's singer elsewhere (1 Chronicles 16:38 and the title of Psalm 39). The difference is one vowel letter.

p: The margin has Unni, the letters Unno.

readings.w: Qere (the reading in the margin of the Masoretic Text); KJV
readings.en: Unni

readings.w: Ketiv (the letters written in the Masoretic Text)
readings.en: Unno

why: Unni is a Levite singer's name in 1 Chronicles 15:18 and 1 Chronicles 15:20. The difference is one letter.

p: The letters read Malluchi, the margin Melicu. The house is Malluch's of 12:2.

readings.w: Ketiv (the letters written in the Masoretic Text); BSB
readings.en: Malluchi

readings.w: Qere (the reading in the margin of the Masoretic Text); KJV (Melicu)
readings.en: Melicu

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (Μαλουχ)
readings.en: Malluch

why: The two Hebrew forms transpose two letters. The written Malluchi is closer to Malluch of 12:2, the house this line continues, and to the Greek Malouch, so it has other support and the Plain follows it, by book.json's policy for names. The setting card for 12:1–26 sets the two priestly lists side by side.

p: The margin has Iddo, the house of 12:4. The letters spell a form like Adaia.

readings.w: Qere (the reading in the margin of the Masoretic Text); KJV
readings.en: Iddo

readings.w: Ketiv (the letters written in the Masoretic Text)
readings.en: Adaia

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (Αδαι)
readings.en: Addai

why: Here the written form has the Greek behind it (Αδαι), but the list itself decides the case: 12:12–21 runs in the order of 12:1–7, where Iddo stands in this place, so the margin is surely right about the house meant, and the written Adaia and the Greek look like one early slip copied twice. The Plain follows the Qere because the parallel list outweighs the Greek here.

p: Among the trumpeters the Hebrew has Miniamin. 2 Esdras has Benjamin.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: Miniamin

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (Βενιαμιν)
readings.en: Benjamin

why: The two names look and sound alike, and the Greek also has Benjamin for Miniamin at 12:17. Miniamin (Mijamin) is a priestly name (10:7; 12:5), which fits a list of priests.

p: The Hebrew names the choir's leader, Jezrahiah. 2 Esdras has "and they were mustered" in his place.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: with Jezrahiah their overseer

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ ἐπεσκέπησαν)
readings.en: and they were mustered

why: The Greek seems to have read the word for "overseer" (paqid) as a verb from the same root, "muster, inspect," and to have dropped the name, as it often drops names in these lists (see the note on 11:16).

a: there were heads of the singers
t: "Heads of the singers" or "Asaph was head"?
p: The margin reads "heads" (plural). The letters read "head," a single chief of the singers; the Greek also has the singular.

readings.w: Qere (the reading in the margin of the Masoretic Text); KJV
readings.en: there were chief of the singers
readings.plain: there were heads of the singers

readings.w: Ketiv (the letters written in the Masoretic Text); Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς πρῶτος τῶν ᾀδόντων)
readings.en: there was a chief of the singers
readings.plain: there was a chief of the singers

why: With the written letters the verse says that in the days of David and Asaph there was a chief of the singers. Some commentators go further and drop the "and" before Asaph, reading "in the days of David, Asaph was chief of the singers," which fits 1 Chronicles 16:5; that is an emendation, not a reading of any manuscript. The margin's plural makes a general statement about leaders of the choirs. The sense is close either way, and the Plain follows the Qere.

a: and in the days of Nehemiah
p: 2 Esdras has "all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel" and no "and in the days of Nehemiah."

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008); KJV
readings.en: and in the days of Nehemiah
readings.plain: and in the days of Nehemiah

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (καὶ πᾶς Ισραηλ ἐν ἡμέραις Ζοροβαβελ)
readings.orig: καὶ πᾶς Ισραηλ ἐν ἡμέραις Ζοροβαβελ
readings.en: and all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel

why: A scribe's eye could easily have skipped from one "in the days of" to the next, which would explain the Greek. Or the Greek may keep an older form, to which a later editor added Nehemiah's name, as some think was done at 8:9 and 12:36. Every Hebrew manuscript has the phrase, and the Plain follows it. The note on this verse discusses what the pairing means.

p: The Hebrew speaks of the "defilements" of the priesthood. 2 Esdras reads the same root as "kinship": the priests' family ties.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008) (גָּאֳלֵי); KJV
readings.en: because they have defiled the priesthood

readings.w: Septuagint, 2 Esdras (Esdras B, the literal Greek of Ezra–Nehemiah), Rahlfs' text, checked (ἐπὶ ἀγχιστείᾳ τῆς ἱερατείας)
readings.en: for the kinship of the priesthood
readings.plain: how they dealt with the kinship of the priesthood

why: Hebrew has two verbs spelled ga'al: one means "defile," the other "act as next of kin, redeem." The Greek took the second, which fits the marriage of 13:28, but the Hebrew vowels and the line's sense of rebuke favor "defilements." The Plain follows the Hebrew. (In 13:31 the Greek has "our God" for "my God," which changes nothing.)
